newsitem.title: UK: London Exchange plays down survey findings.
newsitem.headline: London Exchange plays down survey findings.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange (LSE) on Tuesday played down the findings of a survey that found UK fund managers remained sceptical about the benefits of order-driven share trading, to be introduced this autumn.

"From our own evidence, looking at how the order book works around the world," said a spokesman for the Exchange, "there is enough evidence to show there is higher liquidity, faster trading and tighter spreads that lead to lower dealing costs."
"You can't please everyone all the time but we believe it will offer benefits to large and small investors."

Earlier a poll for Reuters by Tempest Consultants found that most fund managers still believe the order-driven share trading regime will either make no difference to liquidity and speed of execution or will make them worse.

Order-driven trading, where shares are bought automatically and sold via computer instead of being dealt by a market-maker as at present, is intended to bring London into line with bourses overseas and improve its competitiveness.
Yet the results of the survey showed that fund managers remain sceptical of the benefits they will derive from the innovation, just as they were when it was first proposed over a year ago.
The survey findings were part of an annual poll of fund managers giving their ratings of individual stock analysts.
